summary: The candidate is a useful but partial final-ISA analysis feature. Its advertised focused and gfx950 GPU tests pass, but independent valid-assembly cases show that the analyzer's claimed exact opcode counts can contain both false positives and false negatives. Five other major portions of the original six-part request remain unimplemented.

tests.what_was_measured: Confirmed the prepared source tree was imported and reproduced the base absence as ModuleNotFoundError: No module named flydsl.tools.
At exact candidate commit: 29 passed and 2 skipped, covering the candidate regressions and compatibility tests.
Two tests passed on one MI350X/gfx950, including numerical agreement with the portable GPU implementation and final-ISA shape assertions.
The exact candidate reproduced its checked-in retained-ISA JSON report.

A multiline block comment containing instruction-like text was incorrectly reported as three instructions (including one MFMA and one VMEM store), while 'entry: s_nop 0' was incorrectly reported as zero instructions.

gpu_execution_evidence: reports/j-8d21a3dd9942/raw/candidate-gpu.log records two passing tests on the prepared AMD Instinct MI350X/gfx950 path.
remaining_counterexamples: Valid multiline /* ... */ assembly comments cause instruction and family-count false positives.
A valid label and instruction on the same line, such as 'entry: s_nop 0', causes an instruction-count false negative.
Physical VGPR/SGPR pinning or named register-region reservation remains unimplemented.
Exact hand-scheduled region preservation and MFMA co-execute-window assertions remain unimplemented.
The requested first-class AMD instruction helpers remain unimplemented.
The requested exact low-level buffer load/store API remains unimplemented.
The requested compiler-option sweep example remains unimplemented.
remaining_limitations: Only one MI350X/gfx950 GPU path was available; no other CDNA or RDNA architecture was tested.
No native rebuild was performed because the candidate changes no C++/MLIR native source.
Static parsing does not verify cycles, dependencies, occupancy, scheduling guarantees, register pinning, or performance parity with handwritten kernels.
The candidate's GPU tests exercise an existing reduction kernel, not a full attention kernel or the issue's native-ISA performance comparison.
